predecessors.note: The Provisional Government page (infobox 'Preceded by') gives 'Free France' first among the states the Provisional Government follows, with Vichy France and the German administrations; the Free French row of Cliopatria runs 1940..1944 and this row begins in 1945.

correction.text: metropolitan France and its Caribbean and Guianan departments without the occupation zones: 'Three German states (Land) were established: Rheinland Pfalz ... Württemberg-Hohenzollern and South Baden. The zone also included the Saargebiet' and 'Vorarlberg and North Tyrol were assigned to the French Zone' are occupied land, hatched through the occupation events

keyframe_review.note: 711,492 km2: the shape contains metropolitan France plus French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique (no Reunion) and the whole French zone of Germany (Baden-Wuerttemberg and Rheinland-Pfalz cells), the Saar, North Tyrol and Vorarlberg and one Berlin cell. Occupied land is not territory (rule 4), so the zones are removed here and come back as occupation_start events in 1945. Infobox: '1946 (including colonies): 14,200,000 km2' against 698,587 km2 for the 1946 shape: ratio 0.05, because Cliopatria draws the colonies as separate rows (French Africa up to 11.7 M km2, French Indochina), not because the shape is small.

correction.text: metropolitan France and its overseas departments; the French zone of Germany stays occupied land and the Saar, separated from the zones on 16 February 1946 ('France established the separate Saar Protectorate'), is a protectorate in the lighter tint; Réunion ('became a département d'outre-mer (overseas département) of France on 19 March 1946') is added, because it is in no Cliopatria shape

keyframe_review.note: 698,587 km2. Cliopatria drops the Austrian zone in 1946 although the French occupied North Tyrol and Vorarlberg until 1955 ('on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops'): that zone is restored as occupation in the ledger. The shape still holds the German zone and the Saar as French land; both are taken out here (occupation and protectorate events). The 226 cells the shape holds inside Germany include the French-sector Berlin cell (52.54 N 13.28 E), which is occupied land, not French land. Réunion (10 cells) is absent from the shape and is added from 19 March 1946 (Réunion page; ledger gain).

keyframe_review.note: 698,383 km2 for 1947-48 (one cell different from 1946). The Treaty of Paris cession of Tende and La Brigue is two grid cells, one of which the 1946 shape already draws as French (and the Italian shape also draws it), so the shape barely changes; the ledger carries the cession. The Saar customs union with France took effect on 1 April 1948 (Saar page), which does not move the line.

correction.text: as 1947-48; on 23 May 1949 'the three western zones were merged to form the Federal Republic of Germany' and the French zone ceases to be occupied land in the ledger; plus Réunion, an overseas department since 19 March 1946

keyframe_review.note: 698,362 km2, identical in extent to 1947-48. The zone is still in the shape and is taken out as above; Cliopatria removes it only in 1950.

correction.text: metropolitan France and its overseas departments (1950-1955); the Saar, whose constitution took effect on 17 December 1947 and which entered the customs union with France on 1 April 1948, is a protectorate in the lighter tint, not French land; the other cells the shape holds in Germany (the French sector of Berlin among them) are occupied land and are taken out too

keyframe_review.note: 648,243 km2 for 1950-55. The shape still holds 20 cells inside Germany (resolve of the shape intersected with Germany): the Saar (11 cells) and nine others, namely the French-sector Berlin cell (52.54 N 13.28 E), two Lindau / Lake Constance cells, two Upper Rhine border cells and four cells next to the Saarland. The first version of this correction subtracted only the Saarland and so kept those nine as French land; it now subtracts all of Germany, as in 1946-49 (the Saar is a protectorate, the rest is occupied land, Berlin to 1990). Austria's French zone (to October 1955) is occupation in the ledger. Réunion (10 cells) and the Tende circle are added. The page gives France as responsible for foreign affairs and defence of the Saar, hence the protectorate reading rather than annexation.

union.text: Réunion, an overseas department from 19 March 1946

correction.text: metropolitan France and its overseas departments, 1956-1957; the Saar leaves the protectorate on 1 January 1957 when 'Saarland became a West German state' after the Saar Treaty of 27 October 1956; the other cells the shape holds in Germany (the French sector of Berlin among them) are occupied land and are taken out too

keyframe_review.note: 648,243 km2 for 1956-57, same as 1950-55. The same 20 cells inside Germany (the Saar and nine others, the French-sector Berlin cell among them) are taken out; the earlier version of this correction subtracted only the Saarland. It also dropped the Tende / La Brigue circle that 1947-1950 carry, so cell 44.16 N 7.68 E would have left France in 1956 with no event; no event returns Tende to Italy, so the circle is back. Réunion (10 cells) is added. The 1957 part of the shape still contains the Saar although it joined the Federal Republic on 1 January 1957; the vassal_end in the ledger handles it. The Fourth Republic itself ends in October 1958 (page), one year after Cliopatria's last shape; the Fifth Republic row starts in 1958.

region.text: metropolitan France with French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique, as Cliopatria's 1945 row draws it

ledger.note: 1945: the republic that becomes the Fourth Republic governs a liberated France. The Provisional Government of the French Republic 'was officially created by the CFLN on 3 June 1944', moved back to the capital after the liberation of Paris on 25 August 1944 (Paris de facto capital from 31 August 1944) and lasted until the Fourth Republic of 27 October 1946 (Provisional Government page; infobox 'Preceded by: Free France'). The dossier still starts in 1945, the year Cliopatria first draws all of metropolitan France as one row: 1944 is the last shape of the Free French row (89,085 km2, the liberated part), which the free-french dossier owns, so a 1944 start here would cover the same land twice. The Fourth Republic page itself dates the republic 'from 27 October 1946'. Confidence stays 1: the 1945 year is the seam between two Cliopatria rows, not a page's date.

region.text: the French sector of Berlin: West Berlin 'consisted of the American, British, and French occupation sectors established in 1945'

ledger.note: 1945: the French sector of Berlin. The West Berlin page gives the year only ('established in 1945'); its 'In the French sector' heading is empty, so no district is named, and the Allied-occupied Germany page says Berlin 'was jointly occupied by the Allied powers and subdivided into four sectors'. The occupation ran to the unification of Germany: West Berlin 'remained under military occupation until 3 October 1990, the day of unification' (West Berlin), 'de jure continued to be under Allied occupation of the four countries until the reunification of Germany in October 1990' (Allied-occupied Germany). It did not end with the Federal Republic on 23 May 1949 or the western occupation of 5 May 1955. The land is the one Berlin cell (52.54 N 13.28 E) that every Cliopatria shape of this row holds (1945 to 1957). There is no occupation_end here because the occupation outlasts the Fourth Republic; the successor french-fifth-republic carries it to 3 October 1990.

region.text: the French zone: 'Three German states (Land) were established: Rheinland Pfalz ... Württemberg-Hohenzollern and South Baden'; 'control over cities west of the Rhine such as Mainz and Koblenz'; the Berlin cell is split out as its own event

ledger.note: July 1945: the French zone in south-west Germany takes shape. 'In July, the French relinquished Stuttgart to the Americans' and took the cities west of the Rhine; 'The zone also included the Saargebiet.' Potsdam (2 August 1945) divided Germany into four zones; the page gives the Berlin Declaration of 5 June 1945 as the start of the occupation, and no day for the French sector of Berlin. The French-sector Berlin cell is not part of this zone event: Berlin stayed occupied to 1990 and has its own 1945 event.

region.text: 'Vorarlberg and North Tyrol were assigned to the French Zone'

ledger.note: July 1945: the French zone of Austria. 'On 9 July 1945 the Allies agreed on the borders of their occupation zones'; French troops had crossed the Austrian border on 29 April. Renner's cabinet was 'recognized by the Western allies' on 20 October 1945.

region.text: the Saar, separated from the Allied zones of occupation as the Saar Protectorate

ledger.note: 16 February 1946: France 'established the separate Saar Protectorate' by separating the Saar from the Allied zones of occupation. Customs controls against Germany followed on 18 December 1946; the Saarland constitution took effect on 17 December 1947 and the customs union with France on 1 April 1948; France handled the Saar's foreign affairs and defence.

region.text: Réunion, which 'became a département d'outre-mer (overseas département) of France on 19 March 1946'

ledger.note: 19 March 1946: Réunion becomes an overseas department. Réunion (10 cells) is in no Cliopatria shape, neither this row's nor French Africa's, so it is added here as land from no mapped state (it was a colony before; the colonies are separate rows or unmapped). Guadeloupe, Martinique and French Guiana are already in the shape from 1945; the pages opened give no day for them (the Overseas departments and regions page only says they 'were defined as overseas departments' under the 1947 Constitution), so only Réunion's day is on a page.

27 October 1946: the Provisional Government of the French Republic gives way to the Fourth Republic. The page: the republic governed France 'from 27 October 1946 to 4 October 1958'; infobox 'Constitution adopted: 27 October 1946'.

region.text: 'The Tende and La Brigue valleys were ceded to France' (Alpes-Maritimes, upper Roya valley)

ledger.note: 1947: Italy cedes the Tende and La Brigue valleys to France. The treaties 'were signed on 10 February 1947' and took effect on 15 September 1947; the page does not give the day of the transfer, so September is the treaty's entry into force. The Mont Cenis and Little St Bernard rectifications are not on the page.

region.text: the French zone, merged into the Federal Republic (without the Berlin sector, which stays occupied)

ledger.note: 23 May 1949: the French zone becomes part of West Germany. 'The three western zones were merged to form the Federal Republic of Germany'; the page adds that 'the occupation continued until 5 May 1955' under the Allied High Commission, a residual regime that Cliopatria also drops in 1950. The land passes to federal-republic-of-germany (Rheinland-Pfalz, Baden-Württemberg, apart from the Saar). The French sector of Berlin is not in this region: West Berlin 'remained under military occupation until 3 October 1990' (West Berlin page), so its occupation_start of 1945 has no end in this dossier.

region.text: North Tyrol and Vorarlberg, the French zone

ledger.note: 25 October 1955: the last occupying troops leave Austria. The State Treaty was signed on 15 May 1955 and 'came into force on 27 July 1955'; 'on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops.'

region.text: Saarland, which 'became a West German state' on 1 January 1957

ledger.note: 1 January 1957: the Saar becomes a West German state. The 23 October 1955 referendum rejected the Western European Union statute, 67.7 percent to 32.3 percent; the Saar Treaty of 27 October 1956 let it join under Article 23; economic reunification followed on 6 July 1959. The land passes to federal-republic-of-germany.

region.text: metropolitan France and its overseas departments

ledger.note: October 1958: the Fourth Republic gives way to the Fifth. 'The Fourth Republic was dissolved on 5 October 1958' after the Algiers crisis ('On 29 May 1958, French politicians agreed upon calling on De Gaulle'); infobox 'New constitution adopted: 4 October 1958'.

wars.name: First Indochina War
wars.outcome: The page dates the war from 19 December 1946; at the Geneva Conference of 1954 the Viet Minh gained 'control of Vietnam north of the 17th parallel'.
wars.note: No zone is given: the colony is the separate Cliopatria row french-indochina (1860..1957), not this state's shape. The page gives no dates for Laos and Cambodia.

wars.name: Algerian War
wars.outcome: The war begins on 1 November 1954 and continues past the end of the Fourth Republic; the page gives only the start, the Algiers crisis of 1958 and the call on de Gaulle on 29 May 1958.
wars.note: 'to' 1958 is the end of this state, not of the war (the page does not date its end). Algeria is part of the Cliopatria row french-africa, not of this shape.

certainty.note: Metropolitan France is a treaty-bounded state (Tende and La Brigue by the 1947 treaty); the occupation-zone lines were agreed on 9 July 1945 (Austria) and 1945 (Germany); the Saar frontier is the 1946 separation line.

notes:
Cliopatria row: one row 1945..1957, six shapes. It covers metropolitan France with French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique (no Reunion, Mayotte or Algeria: those sit in the separate rows french-africa and french-indochina, 1846/1860..1957, which other groups own), plus the French zone of Germany to 1949, the Saar to 1957, North Tyrol and Vorarlberg in 1945 only, and a Berlin cell that sits in all six shapes (1945 to 1957). All six verdicts are 'adjust' for the same reasons: occupied land is not territory (rule 4), the Saar is a protectorate (Feb 1946 to Jan 1957), and the Austrian zone is missing 1946-55.

Unsettled or outside the page budget: (1) Réunion: it 'became a département d'outre-mer (overseas département) of France on 19 March 1946' (Réunion page); the Fourth Republic page and the Overseas departments and regions page give no date, and Guadeloupe, Martinique and French Guiana, already in the shape, have no day on a page opened. Réunion (10 cells) is in no Cliopatria shape, so a gain event and the corrections from 1946 add it. (2) Morocco and Tunisia independence (1956), the Geneva settlement of 1954, French India (de facto end 1 November 1954) and Cameroon belong to the colonial rows. (3) The French sector of Berlin: West Berlin 'consisted of the American, British, and French occupation sectors established in 1945' and 'remained under military occupation until 3 October 1990' (West Berlin page); the page gives no month and no district. Cliopatria's shapes hold one Berlin cell (52.54 N 13.28 E) in every one of the six years 1945 to 1957; the corrections remove it as occupied land and a 1945 occupation_start keeps it occupied to the end of this dossier (the occupation outlasts the state; the successor french-fifth-republic ends it in 1990). The 1950 and 1956 shapes also hold nine German cells besides the Saar (Berlin, Lindau, the Upper Rhine, next to the Saarland); the corrections now remove all of Germany. (4) Cliopatria's Fourth Republic row ends in 1957 but the republic ends in October 1958; the Fifth Republic row starts 1958. (5) Natural Earth 'France' includes the overseas departments, so a region {country: France} is wider than metropolitan France.

New counterpart dossiers wanted: west-berlin (the French, British and American sectors, 1945..1990), saar-protectorate (1946..1957, a protectorate with its own constitution of 1947), allied-occupied-germany (1945..1949, the occupied owner of the zones, or the zones as separate occupation entities). Gazetteer names wanted: Tende and La Brigue (the 12 km radius around 7.6 E 44.08 N is the researcher's encoding of the two valleys, not a page's coordinates).

The 'Provisional Government of the French Republic' (preceded-by on the page) is treated as the same state (rename on 27 October 1946), not as a separate dossier.
